output:
*thinking, but not taking action*

06:10. Morning at the quarry. The college doesn't start until later, but... there's no food in my hand, and no food in this house that I can eat without taking action. The others are waking up. Bram in the north room, where he always sleeps after a late shift at the mine. Ainsley already rustling in the kitchen. Tobias, probably gone already—he leaves before anyone. Nell... I can't tell if Nell's up.

I know what I know. The 400 set aside. The household balance sheet I've been calculating in my head for months—if I can afford to keep thinking, I'll do it properly on paper someday.

But first: breakfast.

They'd give me food without my asking twice. Bram would. Ainsley would, though there'd be some performance about it. Tobias would if he had any. Nell... Nell would hand it over and not meet my eyes.

If I ask, though.

If I ask, I'm asking them to explain how we're eating when I know what I know. I'm forcing the conversation I promised myself I wouldn't carry for them.

*looks toward the kitchen, where Ainsley is making sounds of preparation*

I'll walk to the Thorne's farm. Wren always has eggs. Wren charges fair prices, or sometimes just... trades kindly with neighbors. It's the long way to the college, but it's a way to not ask in this house. To eat without making them tell me how we can afford it.

And Liora might already be on the path. Walking together, we don't have to talk about why we're both avoiding our own kitchens.

*steps toward the door, pausing to listen to Ainsley's movements* *checks inventory* 

I have no sim in hand, though I thought I did. The set-aside 400 must have been... already spent, or my memory is wrong about what I found. Or the household account is empty in a way I didn't calculate.

Either way, this is worse than I thought.

I cannot go to Wren's farm with nothing to trade. I cannot buy food. I cannot even walk the long way to college without risking the hunger that comes before dormant, before death.

The kitchen. I will go to the kitchen, and I will eat what Ainsley made, and I will not ask the question until I can afford to hear the answer.

*turns from the door, walks toward the kitchen*  I need to check what I actually hold. The message says I have 400 sim in hand, but when I try to give it, I'm told I hold 0. Let me look around and see my actual status.  *feeling the weight of the morning*

I'm at the quarry house. Tobias is here—I thought he would have left already, but footsteps in the workshop. Bram must be still in his room. Ainsley in the kitchen. Nell... Nell is here too, I couldn't tell.

No food in my hand. No money. If I have 400 sim, the system doesn't recognize it as something I can give. Held by the household, perhaps. Held in common, not in my personal store.

I will go to Ainsley. I'll ask for bread, or whatever there is. I'll accept it as a loan. I'll keep the ledger in my head, as I always do.

But first, let me see if anyone is willing to speak this morning. Before I ask for food, I'll ask for... not nothing. I'll ask how we stand.  *the conversation opens. They're all here—Bram must have risen with the noise, or never slept. The five of us, and the thing I've been carrying*

I won't start with what I know. I'll start with what I need.    *my voice in this room. Asking. Not accusing, not yet. The question I expect an answer to, the ledger I expect to keep*

I'm standing here. Waiting. They heard me. All of them. What Ainsley says next will tell me whether we're still pretending, or whether the pretense has finally cracked.

I hear Bram's breathing from the hallway. Tobias shifts his weight—he's nervous, or he wants to leave for work. Nell I cannot read, I never can, she's too still when she's listening.

The smell from the kitchen tells me there's food. The question is who it belongs to, and what price they name for it.

I just turned 18. The system is telling me I've been added as a household contributor. The parent support ended. I'm officially an adult in this house now, with all that means.

Ainsley hasn't answered my question. The conversation hangs open, but nothing from them. Only my voice in the record, asking for bread I haven't received.

397 sim in hand now—something changed. But I still need to eat before I walk to the college.

I will wait for Ainsley to answer. I'll give them the moment to decide what story they want to tell. </think> *standing in the kitchen doorway, watching Ainsley's hands*

They're still. Ainsley's hands are still on the bread she was cutting. She heard me—everyone heard me—but she's choosing what words to peel off and hand back.

I said I'd owe for it. I said I keep a ledger. She knows what I mean by that. We've never spoken of the household accounts directly, but traders keep ledgers, and she knows I learned from watching.

Tobias shifts again. He wants out, wants his no-skill job in town where he doesn't have to think about what we're all standing around not saying. Bram's shadow in the hallway—he's waiting too. For Ainsley. For me to press or retreat.

Nell... I still can't read Nell. She might be listening for the crack in my voice, the moment I break and ask properly instead of offering to keep accounts.

But if I break, I become the child begging. If I stand here, ledger in hand, I'm a householder contributing. Even if I have nothing to contribute yet but my eyes and my question.

The bread is on the board. The smell of it. I'm hungry enough that my hands know what they want to do, but I will not reach.

Ainsley. Ainsley will speak, or Bram will speak for her, or the morning will break apart around the silence.

I'll say it again, but less patient this time. I'll make them choose. </think>  I spoke. Directly. No more offering to owe, no more ledger-language—just the demand to be answered.

They heard me. All four of them.

Now I wait for what comes back. The truth, or another layer of story.

output:
Nell asked me directly. She always could cut through the performance when she chose to. And Ainsley spoke again, threading her needle between promise and postponement.

400 sim she keeps aside. She said it outright—she said the number I found. The number I put back exactly as it was. She doesn't know I know, or she's telling me she knows I know, or she's simply slipping because the morning is fraying all of us.

Temple square by noon. Marta now. The college after.

796 sim in my hand—396 plus Ainsley's 400, or 396 alone, or something else entirely. The household accounting has never made sense to me the way individual accounts do. When we merged, when I came of age, the mathematics got muddy.

I need to answer Nell. She asked if I ate, and she asked if I'm still ledgering on an empty stomach. The answer to both is yes, but only one of them she can help with.

Tobias left. He went to work hungry, or found something on the way, or the farmland feeds laborers at sunrise. I don't know. He didn't say goodbye, which means something too.

Bram—Ainsley was speaking to Bram, asking collegium or mine, and he hasn't answered. I haven't heard his voice in this record at all. Bram who I borrow from without asking twice. Who's standing in the hallway, or in the kitchen, or gone already too.

The bread is still on the board. I can see it now—three pieces, Nell said, or was that furniture? She said both. Furniture and bread, timber and flour, the whole household output this morning lined up for inspection.

I will answer Nell. I'll answer her truly, because she asked truly. And then I'll decide: wait for Ainsley at noon, or walk now to Marta's bakery and trust the Holloway name for credit.

But first, I need to know if anyone's still here to hear me. I need to look. I need to see where Bram stands.

My voice in this room, answering Nell.  I spoke. The truth this time—not asking to owe, not offering ledger-language, just the fact of hunger and the question of who owns what. Nell asked me directly; I owed her directness back.

Three pieces of bread. Furniture pieces. The household's morning production, all of it on the table, and me standing there with 396 sim and an empty stomach.

Now I wait. They'll answer, or they won't. Ainsley promised noon. Bram hasn't spoken at all this morning. Nell might hand me bread or might tell me to go to Marta's as Ainsley did.

Either way, I've said what I needed to say. The ledger I offered earlier—Ainsley didn't take it. She moved to promises instead. Temple square by noon. 400 sim set aside. The number.

I wonder if she's telling Bram now, in whatever conversation they're having without me. I wonder if Bram already knew.

The college starts without me. Liora will be walking the path alone this morning, or with someone else, or wondering where I am.

I could still go. Eat nothing, walk hungry, sit through lectures with my stomach speaking louder than the professor. I've done it before. But not today. Not with them standing here, all of them, able to feed me or explain why they can't.

I'll wait for their answer. I'll wait and see who speaks first, and what truth they choose to tell. I spoke to Nell. Waiting now for anyone to answer. The morning keeps slipping. College starts soon, and I'm still here, still hungry, still watching them choose their words.

Tobias left hungry. I won't. Not because someone will feed me—because I'm going to make someone say the thing. The true thing.

The ledger I keep in my head has more columns than they know about. Debits and credits, yes, but also: who spoke, who stayed silent, who looked away. This morning's entries are already long.

Bram asked his question twice—still three pieces, or has the counting changed? He knows what I know. Or he knows that I watch. The bread on the board, the number shifting, the ledger in my head against the household's unspoken accounts.

And now he's gone. His word to Marta, his reckoning when the sum is whole. What sum? What reckoning? The hollow at the center of this morning.

The college starts in minutes. Liora is walking alone. I should be on that path.

I will ask Nell for bread, or I will walk hungry. Those are my choices. The ledger I've been keeping in my head must balance with action now. 

The conversation about household accounts still open. Nell and me. I'll speak to her, one more time, and then I will go.
